# Heads and assigners

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set head=</code><code class="gp-chip">--set assigner=</code><span class="gp-chip">14 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The head bundle predicts the grasp at every seed: in-plane rotation, depth, width and score. The
assigner matches every seed with the grasp labels it is trained on.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set head=swad-focal -o graspnet-baseline_swad-focal.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list head
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set head=swad-focal -o gsnet_swad-focal.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list head
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set head=swad-focal -o scale-balanced-grasp_swad-focal.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list head
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set head=swad-focal -o economicgrasp_swad-focal.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list head
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set head=swad-focal -o finegrasp_swad-focal.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list head
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#head) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#head) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#head) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#head) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#head).

<!-- method-options:end -->

An assigner is set the same way, `--set assigner=<option>`.

A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: out of the methods under which the swap ran, those under which every comparable loss term ended within the method's tolerance of the component it ships, with nothing rising; a method left out is named with why. Measured on 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.
    - [How we measure](../evidence/index.md) defines every word of these columns.

    Who is left out, and why:

    - `economic-focal`, runs: not GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp (incompatible by design).

    - `NearestLabelAssigner`, runs: own in GSNet; not EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp (incompatible by design).
    - `NearestLabelAssigner`, trains like shipped: not comparable under GraspNet-baseline; diverging under Scale-Balanced-Grasp.

## Choosing

- **A head is swapped whole.** Its network, target encoder, loss and decoder share one way of
  writing a grasp. Its loss terms are swapped one by one on [Losses](losses.md).
- **Head, assigner and labels go together.** A head is trained on dense label grids or on
  compact best grasps; compose switches the assigner and the dataset section to the head's
  label set and says so.
- **The crop decides the head.** A head reads one feature per seed or one per depth bin;
  [Grouper](grouper.md) lists which crop gives which.
- **Classify or regress depth and width:** `decoupled-grid-class` and
  `decoupled-grid-regression` are the two ends; `decoupled-grid-bins` predicts the width as a
  distribution.
- **Scores of two heads are not comparable.** A score threshold fitted to one head does not
  carry over to another.

## Details

??? note "Input and output of a head bundle"

    ```python
    class HeadBundle(nn.Module):
        def forward(self, crops: GroupFeatures) -> Predictions: ...        # raw outputs, with gradients
        def encode(self, matched: MatchedLabels, ...) -> Targets: ...      # labels -> targets
        def loss(self, predictions, targets, ...) -> dict[str, Tensor]:    # named, weighted terms
        def decode(self, raw, seeds, approach, gripper) -> GraspGroup: ... # one grasp per seed
    ```

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | in: crop features | from the grouper, one row per valid seed, with the grouper's `out_axes`: `('seed', 'channel')` or `('seed', 'depth', 'channel')`. |
    | in: matched labels | from the assigner, reduced to the chosen view: `dense` (a friction and a width per in-plane angle and depth bin) or `compact` (one best grasp per seed). |
    | out, training | named loss terms, each multiplied by its `weight`; the trainer sums them and logs each as `loss/<name>`. |
    | out, prediction | a `GraspGroup` with one grasp per seed: translation (the seed), rotation (approach from the view stage, in-plane angle from the head), depth, width (metres), score. |

    | Attribute | Meaning | Rule |
    |---|---|---|
    | `in_axes` | axes of the crop features it expects | must equal the grouper's `out_axes` |
    | `label_format` | `dense` or `compact` | must equal the assigner's (and the dataset must serve that label set) |
    | `score_kind` | meaning of the decoded score | scores of different kinds are not comparable |
    | `applies_seed_weights` | whether its loss honours a weight per seed | an assigner that returns weights needs a head that applies them |
    | `loss_terms` | loss option → kind of term | every loss node is checked against it ([Losses](losses.md)) |

??? note "The assigner"

    The assigner runs in training only. It matches every seed with the labels of the label
    point it sits on and hands them, reduced to the chosen view, to the view stage and the head.
    So it is chosen with the head and the label set, not on its own.

    - `NearestLabelAssigner` (its defaults, no preset): every seed takes the labels of the
      nearest label point of its object; every seed is supervised.
    - `nearest-label-object-seeds`: the same matching; only seeds on an object are supervised,
      and training crops sit at the matched label point.
    - `compact-label`: one labelled grasp per seed at its chosen view, only within 5 mm of a
      label point; it brings the dataset section `compact_labels`.
    - `scale-balanced`: the matching above plus a loss weight per seed, larger for rare grasp
      widths. It needs the width histogram of the training split
      (`grasppanda prepare graspnet1b --scale-statistic`; `configs/scale_balanced_grasp/README.md`);
      compose adds the dataset section `scale_statistic` and says so.

    `grasppanda compose --show assigner=scale-balanced` prints a preset with what must be
    re-tuned.

??? note "The settings of `DecoupledGridHead`"

    ```yaml
    model:
      head:
        type: DecoupledGridHead
        num_angle: 12
        num_depth: 4
        depth_step: 0.01
        depth: class                  # class | regression (a continuous depth between the bins)
        width: bins                   # regression | class (bin centre) | bins (expectation)
        width_bins: 16                # for class and bins: 16 over 0.1 m is a bin every 6.7 mm
        score_target: log_friction_fixed_range
        friction_range: [0.1, 1.0]    # the range of the GraspNet-1Billion labels
        width_loss: {type: DistributionFocal, weight: 1.0}
    ```

    - The kind of `depth_loss` and `width_loss` follows the options `depth` and `width`, so a
      loss must change with them (the presets do).
    - The class terms start near ln 12 and ln 4, a regressed width is a distance in metres × 10:
      watch `loss/angle` and `loss/depth` beside `loss/score` and re-tune the weights.
    - `width_decode_gain: 1.2` opens the gripper 20 % wider than learned, as the other heads of
      the family do; 1.0 decodes what was learned.
    - A head and a loss combine: `--set head=decoupled-grid --set head.score_loss=varifocal`.

    `DecoupledGridHead` is written here after the idea of the grasp head of FGC-GraspNet
    ([arXiv 2206.11141](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11141), ICRA 2022), without its code. No head
    has released weights of its own.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **A label set is a contract.** Compose switches the labels and the assigner for a head
      of the other label set, and the dense grids then come from the label store of
      `grasppanda prepare <dataset> --labels`. A config written by hand with a mismatch is
      refused:

        ```text
        ✗ assigner · head: CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but
          DecoupledGridHead is supervised with 'dense' ones. A head bundle and the assigner
          that feeds it must agree on the label set; the dataset must serve that label set too.
        ```

    - **A logit loss changes what the score is.** A score threshold fitted on the unbounded
      score of `swad` does not carry over to `swad-focal`, whose score lies in [0, 1].
    - **`SWADHead` with `score_target: log_friction_batch_norm`** (the GSNet reference)
      normalises targets with the extrema of the batch; `log_friction_fixed_range` gives a target
      that means the same in every batch (`swad-focal` sets it).
    - **The extra class of `EconomicHead`.** With `unmatched_class: true` every classifier has
      one output that is never supervised; label smoothing gives it target mass. Use
      `decode_argmax: supervised` (as `economic-focal` does) or `unmatched_class: false`.
    - **Seed weights.** A stage that receives the weights of `ScaleBalancedAssigner` must apply
      them (`applies_seed_weights`); a loss that scores the supervised set as a whole cannot, so
      it is refused there ([Losses](losses.md)).

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | The grasp head of [FGC-GraspNet](https://github.com/luyh20/FGC-GraspNet) as code | no licence file, and it derives from graspnet-baseline (non-commercial); its idea is `DecoupledGridHead`, written here. |
    | Heads of graspnet-baseline and its descendants as code | a non-commercial licence; the ported heads are written from papers and behaviour. |
    | Contact-GraspNet's per-point contact head | an NVIDIA non-commercial licence. |
    | A decoupled head for depth-bin crops or for compact labels | `DecoupledGridHead` reads dense label grids and one feature per seed; under the other methods compose changes their labels or crop for it. |
